title: Token choreography: entropy-driven slice allocation and attention-head pruning for balanced latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: As tenant workloads diversify (short-chat bursts, long-form completions, high-embedding preprefill batches), our current prefill/decode partitioning tends to either fragment microbatches (hurting throughput) or create large phase windows (hurting tail latency). This ticket explores a new policy that combines an entropy-driven token slicing heuristic with selective attention-head pruning to reduce per-token kernel cost while preserving semantics for latency-sensitive requests. Goals: 1) reduce median and 95th percentile latency for small- to medium-length requests by 15-30% on p3x-like hardware under mixed-tenant workloads; 2) maintain overall throughput within 95% of baseline for large batches; 3) provide knobs for tenant fairness (latency-first vs throughput-first). Acceptance criteria: - A configurable slice allocator that uses a lightweight per-request entropy estimate to choose split points and bundle candidates. - Attention-head pruning module that activates only for slices whose entropy indicates low head-sensitivity (configurable threshold). - Kernel-aware bundling that groups slices by estimated kernel latency profile (fp16 vs quantized kernel preference). - End-to-end benchmark demonstrating latency improvements on the mixed workload harness and a controlled degradation <5% in output quality (as measured by a small eval set). - Documented rollout plan and safety guardrails (canary + forced fallback to baseline).
implementation_notes: 2025-11-13: Spike completed — implemented lightweight Shannon-entropy estimator on request prefixes. Early microbench shows good correlation between low entropy and robustness to dropping top attention heads.
2025-11-18: Integrated entropy estimator into allocator prototype. Added kernel hints (expected_kernel: 'fp16_fast' or 'int8_qkv') derived from sequence length and token-type metadata.

2025-11-22: Implemented attention-head pruning hook in runtime; runtime toggles pruning per-slice with a policy layer. Measured single-slice decode cost reduction of ~18% when pruning 2 of 16 heads on base-1 parameters.
2025-11-27: Built bundler that groups slices by (entropy_bucket, kernel_hint) before submitting to GPU. This reduces small-slice kernel invocation overhead by batching similar kernels together.

2025-12-01: Experiment run against mixed-tenant harness (20% short chat <50 tokens, 50% medium 50-300 tokens, 30% long >300). Observed median latency down 22% and p95 down 16% for latency-first policy; throughput drop ~3% for large-batch-only tests.

2025-12-03: Addressed a correctness regression where pruning impacted subtle QA completions — added fallback: if eval-quality delta > 2% on a rolling prompt-set, disable pruning for that tenant automatically.
decisions: Use Shannon entropy over last 32 token logits as the primary heuristic for slice sensitivity due to low compute cost and strong empirical signal.
Make attention-head pruning conservative: default to at most 2 heads removed for models with >=12 heads; expose knob for experimentation.
Kernel hints will not be prescriptive; allocator emits 'preference' tag and runtime kernel selector finalizes mapping to actual kernels to avoid tight coupling.
Expose two preset policies: 'latency-first' (favor smaller slices + aggressive pruning) and 'throughput-first' (coalesce larger slices, minimal pruning).
tests: Unit: entropy estimator against synthetic distributions (uniform, peaked, multimodal) — expected buckets produced.
Integration: bundler + runtime on single-node GPU; verify grouped kernel invocations have homogeneous kernel_id in traces.
Perf: mixed-tenant harness with 50k requests; capture median/p95 and per-tenant fairness metrics (latency delta vs baseline).
Quality: evaluate on 1k-shot QA/prompt suite; require <5% quality regression for default policy and <2% for canary before tenant rollout.
Canary rollout: 5% traffic for latency-first policy in staging then ramp with automated quality checks and rollback on threshold breach.
risks: Pruning may produce rare semantic regressions for prompts that rely on specific attention heads; mitigated with automatic quality monitoring and fast rollback.
Entropy estimator is an approximation and might correlate poorly for certain tokenizers or multilingual inputs — we must validate on production prompt samples before wide rollout.
Kernel bundling adds scheduling complexity which could interact poorly with existing phase-splitting rules; add integration tests that mirror production shard patterns.
metrics_and_dashboards: Perf board: runtime-2.4/token-choreography - median latency, p95, throughput, GPU-kernel-invocation-count per minute.
Quality alert: token-choreography/auto-quality - rolling eval delta, per-tenant quality regressions.
Fairness view: per-tenant latency delta vs baseline, tenant-weights, and slice-count distribution.
